name: orchestration-request-admission
goal: Refuse provider calls that could cross 190000 active context tokens before issuing the request, then preserve checkpoint handoff and fresh restart.

steps.title: Identify the failing behavior, expected behavior, and reproduction.
steps.evidence: Use a live process fixture with 138000 observed context and 60000 bytes of pending input. The provider request must be stopped before transport and the checkpoint must resume.

steps.title: Explain why existing standardized tests missed the bug; name the scenario, fixture, lifecycle or assertion gap and reusable test change.
steps.evidence: The previous CLI case monitored provider usage after dispatch. The new normal-entry integration fixture submits a second payload below the handoff threshold and verifies pre-request rotation with separate telemetry.

steps.title: Strengthen the existing standardized test; commit it before repair, run it failing with loop record --phase red, and preserve the assertion.
steps.evidence: Frozen no-gate fixture failed the checkpoint resume assertion before code changes.

steps.title: Implement the smallest repair without weakening the regression test.
steps.evidence: Both provider CLIs route model inputs through the local admission boundary; estimates are stored separately from observed usage.

steps.title: Rerun the same unchanged regression test at a separate fix commit with loop record --phase green; preserve passing proof.
steps.evidence: Unchanged normal-entry regression refused the oversized pending request and completed in a fresh session.

steps.title: Run relevant project checks and affected UI browser flows with fresh inspected screenshots and no unexpected browser errors; preserve diagnostics and keep pending until proof passes.
